concept_html:
Lesson B19-L7 tested code that does I/O by passing the dependency in. A model call is I/O with three extra traits: every call costs money, a call can stop early, and the same prompt can get a different reply each time.

Pass the model in. Pipeline code takes call_model, a function from messages to reply text. Production wraps the SDK client. Tests pass a fake that returns fixed text, so parsing, retries and logging run with no network and no API key.

Check why it stopped. In anthropic 2.4.0 a response has a stop_reason. "end_turn" means the model finished. "max_tokens" means the reply hit your max_tokens limit, so any JSON in it is likely cut off. "refusal" means the model declined. Treat every value except "end_turn" as a failed attempt, never as an answer. Then take the first block whose type is "text".

Cache by everything that shapes the reply. A rerun should not pay again for replies it already has, and should give the same labels. Store each reply under a key built from the model ID, the prompt version and the messages:

text = json.dumps({"model": model, "prompt_version": version, "messages": messages}, sort_keys=True)
key = hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest()

sort_keys=True turns equal dicts into equal text, whatever their key order. hexdigest() returns 64 hex characters. Leave the model ID out and a model upgrade returns old replies without a single new call.

Log every call. Append one record per call to the run log: run_id, a UTC timestamp, model, prompt version, cache hit or miss, stop reason, and the token counts in response.usage.input_tokens and response.usage.output_tokens. Cost and drift then come from data.

The SDK retries some failures for you. anthropic 2.4.0 retries connection errors and status codes 408, 409, 429 and 500 or above, twice by default (max_retries=2). Your code handles what is left: stop reasons and invalid replies.

lines: import hashlib
import json
from collections.abc import Callable, MutableMapping
from typing import Any
def reply_text(response: Any) -> str:
"""Text of a finished reply.
Args:
response: A Message from client.messages.create.
Returns:
The first text block.
Raises:
RuntimeError: If the reply did not finish, or has no text block.
"""
if response.stop_reason != "end_turn":
raise RuntimeError(f"reply stopped early: {response.stop_reason}")
for block in response.content:
if block.type == "text":
return block.text
raise RuntimeError("reply has no text block")
def cache_key(model: str, prompt_version: str, messages: list[dict[str, str]]) -> str:
"""Hash of everything that shapes the reply."""
payload = {"model": model, "prompt_version": prompt_version, "messages": messages}
text = json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True)
return hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest()
def cached_reply(
messages: list[dict[str, str]],
model: str,
prompt_version: str,
call_model: Callable[[list[dict[str, str]]], str],
cache: MutableMapping[str, str],
) -> tuple[str, bool]:
"""Reply from the cache, or from one model call that is then cached.
Returns:
The reply text and True when it came from the cache.
"""
key = cache_key(model, prompt_version, messages)
if key in cache:
return cache[key], True
reply = call_model(messages)
cache[key] = reply
return reply, False

from collections.abc import Callable, MutableMapping


def cached_reply(
    messages: list[dict[str, str]],
    model: str,
    prompt_version: str,
    call_model: Callable[[list[dict[str, str]]], str],
    cache: MutableMapping[str, str],
) -> tuple[str, bool]:
    """Reply from the cache, or from one model call that is then cached.

    Args:
        messages: The prompt messages.
        model: Model ID.
        prompt_version: Version of the prompt file.
        call_model: Takes messages and returns the reply text.
        cache: Stored replies by key.

    Returns:
        The reply text and True when it came from the cache.
    """
    key = cache_key(model, prompt_version, messages)
    if key in cache:
        return cache[key], True
    reply = call_model(messages)
    cache[key] = reply
    return reply, False

title: Model calls in a pipeline, stop reasons, caching and run logs
why_html: A team reran a theme-coding job after fixing a typo in its report code. The rerun called the model again for all 12,000 answers. It paid twice, a few hundred labels changed, and the published wave totals no longer matched the dashboard. A cache keyed on model, prompt version and messages would have reused every reply and kept the labels fixed.
